title: Finite-limit preservation cancels through a reflecting functor
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ be categories and let $F\colon\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $V\colon\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$ be functors. Suppose $V\circ F$ preserves finite limits ([def-galois-finite-limits-colimits]), and $V$ reflects finite limits: whenever the image under $V$ of a cone over a finite diagram in $\mathcal D$ is limiting, that cone is limiting. Then $F$ preserves finite limits. Here a functor preserves finite limits if it sends every limit cone over a finite diagram to a limit cone of the image diagram.
